title: Sequential Bayesian early-stop controller for multi-metric A/B model experiments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: As teams run progressive model upgrades we need a lifecycle controller that can safely decide when to stop, expand, or rollback an experiment without relying on fixed-duration buckets. Current canary/AB tooling in Redwood requires manual monitoring and conservative time windows, which slows rollouts and increases operational burden. This ticket proposes a sequential decision engine that applies Bayesian posterior checks and multi-metric safety budgets to provide automated early-stop and auto-rollback actions, while exposing control knobs to product and platform teams.
background_and_motivation: Why Bayesian sequential checks: sequential experiments produce repeated looks at the data; frequentist tests must be adjusted (alpha-spend) and are brittle with variable traffic. A Bayesian posterior approach with pre-specified decision thresholds simplifies continuous monitoring, naturally handles stopping rules, and integrates well with multi-metric utility functions. We want a controller that: 1) supports primary/guardrail metrics, 2) handles unequal sample sizes across cohorts, 3) integrates with shadow traffic for preflight analysis, and 4) emits explainable reasons for rollbacks for audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: API: ability to create an experiment manifest with primary metric, list of guardrail metrics, safety budgets, and decision rules (posterior thresholds and minimum sample sizes).
Controller: evaluation loop that computes posterior distributions for metric deltas in near-real time and emits decisions: CONTINUE, EXPAND, HALT, AUTO-ROLLBACK.
Console: UI shows live posterior probability curves, sample counts, and the controller's recommended action with rationale and last trigger reason.

Rollout automation: when auto-rollback trigger fires, system performs a reversible rollback and writes a structured audit entry with metric snapshots, posterior values, and links to relevant PRs/dashboards.
Safety budgets: per-customer and per-cohort budgets prevent runaway exposure; controller enforces budget caps and sends alerts when budgets are low.
Testing: integrated simulation harness that runs historical traffic replays and synthetic degradations to validate Type I/II behavior and average time-to-detect for degradation scenarios.
Telemetry: instrumentation for posterior traces, decision timestamps, and per-variant metric streams fed to Cost/Latency/Quality dashboards.
Documentation: PRD and runbook describing configuration knobs, recommended thresholds for typical metrics (e.g., latency, error-rate, quality delta), and post-mortem checklist after an auto-rollback.
metrics_and_stat_checks: Primary metric: chosen by experiment manifest; controller computes posterior on delta = variant - control.
Posterior model: beta-binomial for binary metrics, Gaussian with hierarchical variance for continuous metrics; default weakly-informative priors provided.
Decision rule examples: if P(delta < -eps_primary | data) > 0.95 AND n_samples >= min_n_primary -> AUTO-ROLLBACK; if P(delta > eps_primary | data) > 0.975 -> EXPAND.

Guardrails: evaluate guardrail metrics with asymmetric thresholds (e.g., latency: eps=+50ms, error-rate: eps=+0.5%); a single guardrail breach with P(breach) > 0.9 for sustained window triggers HALT and shadow only.
Sequential controls: minimum look interval (e.g., 5 minutes), minimum n for primary and for guardrails, and exponential backoff on decision cadence when traffic low.
False alarm control: support configurable equivalent of alpha-spend expressed as posterior probability thresholds and minimum exposure before allowing expansion.
Drift detection: KS-test or CUSUM on input feature distributions triggers a shadow analysis job that evaluates model-sample mismatch before any decision to expand.
implementation_notes: Controller will be implemented as a separate service (rollout-controller) that subscribes to per-variant metric streams from metrics-pipeline and KV cache of sample counts.
Leverage existing eval infra (ENG-3178) to run offline posterior checks and simulation harness; expose a lightweight online inference module for low-latency posterior updates.
APIs: POST /experiments (manifest), GET /experiments/:id/status, PATCH /experiments/:id/controls, POST /experiments/:id/rollback to allow manual override.
State machine: EXPERIMENT_STATE {DRAFT, RUNNING, PAUSED, HALTED, ROLLED_BACK, COMPLETED}. Controller transitions must be idempotent and persisted in the control-plane DB.
Audit logging: every auto-decision writes a structured entry to audit-log with decision_reason, posterior_snapshot, and links to related dashboards/PRs.

Scaling: online posterior updates should be batched and use approximate updating (e.g., moment-matching) to avoid per-request heavy compute. Heavy re-computation can be scheduled off the critical path.
ui_changes: Experiment detail page: add 'Posterior view' with probability curves and decision boundary lines; include timeline of decisions and exposures.
Quick action buttons: Pause, Force-rollback, Escalate to SRE with pre-filled context (metric snapshots + links).
Safety budget panel: shows remaining exposure by cohort and estimated days until budget exhaustion at current ramp rate.
Simulation tab: allow product teams to run hypothetical degradations against historical data to preview controller behavior.
api_changes: New resource ExperimentManifest with fields: name, description, primary_metric, guardrails[], min_samples, posterior_thresholds{}, safety_budget{}, shadow_policy{}.
New endpoints for controller control and status streaming (server-sent events) for live posterior traces.
Webhook contract for auto-rollback and alerts to integrators (Slack, PagerDuty, Ops runbook link).
tests_and_eval_harness: Replay harness will replay 6 months of production traffic to validate Type I error (target < 5%) and mean time to detect various degradation magnitudes (±5%, ±20%).
Synthetic stress tests: create adversarial input distributions and latency spikes to ensure guardrail triggers work and shadow-only mode prevents user exposure.
A/B simulation grid: run experiments across sample rates (0.1% to 30%) and cohort skews to surface behavior under low-traffic scenarios.
Automated regression suite tied to PRs that runs a short simulation and checks controller's front-line decisions against golden rules.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): implementation in staging using synthetic traffic, run 2-week smoke to validate infra and telemetry.
Phase 1 (beta): enable controller for internal product teams only, default conservative thresholds; gather feedback for 4 weeks.
Phase 2 (opt-in): expose to selected customers with design/solutions help; provide training and runbooks.
Phase 3 (ga): enable in console as an available option with recommended presets; provide migration guide for existing canary strategies.
Rollback semantics: auto-rollback will trigger a reversible operation that preserves old variant pinning for 24h; manual review required for permanent decommissions.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy posterior estimates at low volumes could lead to false rollbacks. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample thresholds and a low-traffic backoff policy.

Risk: controller complexity increases surface area for bugs that could auto-rollback broadly. Mitigation: default disable auto-rollback for externally visible customers; require opt-in and use safety budgets.
Risk: operational cost for continuous posterior updates. Mitigation: use approximate incremental updates and compute heavy recomputations asynchronously.
Risk: lack of explainability for stakeholders. Mitigation: produce human-readable decision reasons and snapshot attachments in audit logs.
